This [DSPA2 appendix](https://www.socr.umich.edu/DSPA2/) illustrates some very simple examples of using the [OpenAI API](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/OpenAI) for synthetically generating free text, 2D images, and software code.

```{r setup, echo=FALSE, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE)

# Load user-specific OpenAI API Key
# Sys.setenv(OPENAI_API_KEY = 'xxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxx')
# Alternatively, add the key to the .Renviron file of the project. To open .Renviron for editing
# if (!require(usethis))
#     install.packages("usethis")
# usethis::edit_r_environ(scope = "project")

# 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 
library(openai)
Sys.setenv(OPENAI_API_KEY = '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')
```

This is a $3^{rd}$ generation SOCR AI Bot for (1) synthetically simulating intelligent text response to human text/voice prompts; (2) simulating realistic 2D brain images; and (3) writing R code for simple verbal descriptions. These are based on [OpenAI](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/OpenAI) and [Third-generation Generative Pre-trained Transformer (GPT-3)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/GPT-3) technologies.

# Context-Specific Synthetic Text Responses

Based on [GPT3](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/GPT-3), use OpenAI to respond to the following prompt, i.e., the text input seeding/guiding the AI verbose response:

*Expected health disparities and racial inequality in the US in 2030...*

```{r text1}
# What sampling temperature to use. Higher values means the model will take more risks. Try 0.9 for more creative applications, and 0 (argmax sampling) for ones with a well-defined answer.

# GPT-3 models: https://beta.openai.com/docs/models/gpt-3

# General Health Essay
synthText <- create_completion(model = "gpt-3.5-turbo-instruct", n=5, best_of=10,
                               max_tokens=300, temperature=0.8, # 
                               prompt = "Write an abstract of a healthcare essay")
                               # prompt = "How many outerspace layers are there?")
synthText$choices$text

# Health Disparity
synthText <- 
  create_completion(model = "gpt-3.5-turbo-instruct", n=5, best_of=10,
                    max_tokens=300, temperature=0.8, # 
                    prompt = "Expected health disparities and racial inequality in the US in 2030")
synthText$choices$text
```

# Realistic 2D Brain Images

Generate 5 2D sagittal MRI brain images of Alzheimer's disease patients and contrast these to healthy control patients.

## imulated 2D Brain Scans of Asymptomatic Controls (Healthy Participants)

```{r brainImagesHC}
#### Healthy Controls 

library(RCurl)
library(json64)
library(plotly)

# Generate images": maximum text-prompt text length is 1000 characters, 1 <= n <= 10
# https://beta.openai.com/docs/api-reference/images/create

synthImages <- create_image("2D sagittal MRI brain image of Healthy Asymptomatic Controls",
                            n=5, size="1024x1024",
                            response_format="b64_json")  # response_format="url"

# Convert base64 JSON synth images to 2D rasterized images
# single image rendering
# raw1 <- base64Decode(synthImages$data[1]$b64_json[1], mode="raw")
# img1 <- png::readPNG(raw1)
# plot_ly(z=~(255*img1), type="image")
# plot_ly(z=~(255*img1[,,1]), type="heatmap")

convBase64JSON2Img <- function(txt) {
  raw <- base64Decode(txt, mode="raw")
  # Handle PNG format
  if (all(as.raw(c(0x89, 0x50, 0x4e, 0x47, 0x0d, 0x0a, 0x1a, 0x0a)) == raw[1:8])) {
    img <- png::readPNG(raw)
  } 
  # Handle JPEG format
  else if (all(as.raw(c(0xff, 0xd8, 0xff, 0xd9)) == raw[c(1:2, length(raw)-(1:0))])) { 
    img <- jpeg::readJPEG(raw)
  } 
  # Currently no other formats are interpreted, but other formats can be added below
  else stop("No Appropriate Image Format Interpreter Available ...")
  return(img)
}
# raw1 <- convBase64JSON2Img(synthImages$data[1]$b64_json[1])
# plot_ly(z=~(255*raw1), type="image")

vars <- c(1:length(synthImages$data[1]$b64_json))
plots <- lapply(vars, function(var) {
  raw = convBase64JSON2Img(synthImages$data[1]$b64_json[var])
  plot_ly(z=~(255*raw), type="image", name=paste0("Synth Healthy Control Img ", var)) %>%
                        layout(title = paste0("Synth AD Img ", var),
                          xaxis = list(title = "", showticklabels = FALSE), 
                          yaxis = list(title = "", showticklabels = FALSE))
})
subplot(plots, nrows = 1, shareY = TRUE) %>% layout(title="Simulated 2D Scans of Healthy Controls")
```

## Simulated 2D Brain Scans of Alzheimer's Disease Patients

```{r brainImagesAD}
#### AD Patients
# Generate images": maximum text-prompt text length is 1000 characters, 1 <= n <= 10
# https://beta.openai.com/docs/api-reference/images/create

synthImages <- create_image("2D sagittal MRI brain image of Alzheimer's disease",
                            n=5, size="1024x1024",
                            response_format="b64_json")  # response_format="url"

convBase64JSON2Img <- function(txt) {
  raw <- base64Decode(txt, mode="raw")
  # Handle PNG format
  if (all(as.raw(c(0x89, 0x50, 0x4e, 0x47, 0x0d, 0x0a, 0x1a, 0x0a)) == raw[1:8])) {
    img <- png::readPNG(raw)
  } 
  # Handle JPEG format
  else if (all(as.raw(c(0xff, 0xd8, 0xff, 0xd9)) == raw[c(1:2, length(raw)-(1:0))])) { 
    img <- jpeg::readJPEG(raw)
  } 
  # Currently no other formats are interpreted, but other formats can be added below
  else stop("No Appropriate Image Format Interpreter Available ...")
  return(img)
}

vars <- c(1:length(synthImages$data[1]$b64_json))
plots <- lapply(vars, function(var) {
  raw = convBase64JSON2Img(synthImages$data[1]$b64_json[var])
  plot_ly(z=~(255*raw), type="image", name=paste0("Synth AD Img ", var)) %>%
                        layout(title = paste0("Synth AD Img ", var),
                          xaxis = list(title = "", showticklabels = FALSE), 
                          yaxis = list(title = "", showticklabels = FALSE))
})
subplot(plots, nrows = 1, shareY = TRUE) %>% layout(title="Simulated 2D Alzheimer's disease scans")
```


# Automated Software Code Explaining, Modification, De Novo Writing

## Code-to-text Explaining

 - *JavaScript Function 1*: create an array of 100 random uniform values
 - *R Function 2*: for a given sample and a confidence level, compute the confidence interval around mean using normal approximation.

```{r code2text}
# https://beta.openai.com/docs/guides/code/quickstart
# prompt  <- '// Function 1
# var fullNames = [];
# for (var i = 0; i < 100; i++) {
#   fullNames.push(names[Math.floor(Math.random() * names.length)]
#     + " " + lastNames[Math.floor(Math.random() * lastNames.length)]);
# }
# 
# // What does Function 1 do?
# '

prompt  <- '// Function 1
x <- runif(100)
conf = 0.95
se <- sd(x) / sqrt(length(x))
alpha <- 1 - conf
mean(x) + se * qnorm(c(alpha/2, 1 - alpha/2))

// What does Function 1 do?
'

response = create_completion(model="code-davinci-002", prompt=prompt,
                             temperature=0, max_tokens=64, top_p=1.0, frequency_penalty=0.0,
                             presence_penalty=0.0)

response$choices[[1]]
```

## CodeX

The [Codex model](https://beta.openai.com/docs/guides/code/introduction) fine-tunes the [GPT-3 series](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/GPT-3) for software code. It is capable of drafting Python, R, JavaScript, Go, Perl, PHP, Ruby, Swift, SQL, and shell scripts.

This prompt: *Write code to compute the five number summary of a given sample (vector)*, results in the following JavaScript code:

```{r eval=FALSE}
/* write code to compute five number summary of a sample */
var rCode = document.createElement('script');
rCode.innerHTML = 'var x = rnorm(100); var y = rnorm(100); var z = rnorm(100); var w = rnorm(100); var v = rnorm(100); var fiveNum = function(x) { return(c(min(x), quantile(x, 0.25), median(x), quantile(x, 0.75), max(x))); }; fiveNum(x); fiveNum(y); fiveNum(z); fiveNum(w); fiveNum(v);';
document.body.appendChild(rCode);
```

We can also test the code in `R`.

```{r}
x = rnorm(100)
y = rnorm(100)
z = rnorm(100)
w = rnorm(100)
v = rnorm(100)
fiveNum = function(x) { 
  return(c(min(x), quantile(x, 0.25), median(x), quantile(x, 0.75), max(x)))
}
fiveNum(x); fiveNum(y); fiveNum(z); fiveNum(w); fiveNum(v)
```

Of course, this code may need to be properly formatted to make it useful. Yet, this AI-generated skeleton of a function can save significant amount of software development time.
